biodiversity_overview.text: 170,622 GBIF occurrence records for 109 tracked species are attributed to Tamil Nadu, spanning 1829-2026.
162,483 of these records (95.2%) are located to within 10 km.

species_richness.text: Observed tracked species by group: Aves 27, Magnoliopsida 21, Mammalia 19, Actinopterygii 14, Squamata 9, Amphibia 9, Testudines 4, Liliopsida 2, Cephalopoda 2, Crocodylia 1, Elasmobranchii 1.

threatened_species.text: 13 species with records here are officially threatened (IUCN CR/EN/VU). Names and categories from the IUCN Red List export are not shown in this public snapshot.
4 further species are threatened according to the project's unverified reference list: Asian Elephant (EN), Sloth Bear (VU), Tiger (EN), Mugger Crocodile (VU).

notable_species.text: Most recorded species: Indian Roller (17,633), Indian Scimitar-Babbler (15,049), Common Peafowl (13,655), Indian Spot-billed Duck (10,720), Indian Pond-heron (10,387).

temporal_trends.text: Records per year went from 8,967 in 2016 to 1,978 in 2025. This reflects recording effort as much as wildlife and is not a population trend.

protection_coverage.text: Wildlife protected areas (OpenStreetMap national parks, sanctuaries and reserves) cover 4.36% of Tamil Nadu's area (52 areas intersect the state).
10.3% of precisely located records fall inside these areas (16,811 of 162,483); this is not a measure of habitat protection.

risk_indicators.text: Highest model-predicted vulnerability among species recorded here (MODEL PREDICTION, not IUCN status): Toad-skinned Frog (0.69), Indian Star Tortoise (0.61), Carplet (0.55), Indian Scad (0.48), Small Indian Mongoose (0.47).

conservation_priority.text: Top experimental CIPI grid cells in Tamil Nadu (equal-weight reference): cell near 13.125N 80.625E (overall rank 4, median rank across weightings 6); cell near 10.875N 76.875E (overall rank 6, median rank across weightings 11); cell near 7.875N 77.625E (overall rank 11, median rank across weightings 20).

environmental_pressures.text: Tree cover of at least 30% canopy covered 12,063 km2 (9.32% of land) in 2000 (Hansen Global Forest Change; includes plantations).

327.7 km2 of that tree cover was lost in 2001-2024 (2.72% of the 2000 extent; 1.39% in 2015-2024, rank 11 of 35 states). The largest annual loss was in 2024 (29.16 km2). Loss includes plantation harvest and natural disturbance; regrowth is not subtracted.
Built-up surfaces cover 2.16% of land and population density is 632.2 people per km2 (GHSL 2020).
27% of 30 m tree-cover pixels lie on a forest edge (a fragmentation indicator; higher means more fragmented).
These describe pressures on places; they do not show effects on any species.
